raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #36495.

`--speculative-algorithm NGRAM --speculative-ngram-capacity 4 --speculative-ngram-max-trie-depth 4`
is accepted at startup, but the first request that reaches the ngram corpus aborts the scheduler
with `munmap_chunk(): invalid pointer` (`Subprocess scheduler_0 crashed with exit code -6`). With
warmup on (the default), that first request is the warmup request, so the server never becomes
healthy, after the weights are already loaded.

Root cause: the trie takes its root from the same node pool, so only `capacity - 1` nodes are
usable, while inserting one suffix of length `max_trie_depth` can need `max_trie_depth` new nodes.
With `capacity == max_trie_depth`, the first long insert asks `squeeze()` to release one node. The
guard in `squeeze()` counts every in-use node as releasable, including the root (which is never in
`global_lru_`), so it passes, and the loop then calls `global_lru_.back()` on an empty list. Smaller
capacities fail the same guard with an exception that escapes the insert worker thread, which also
terminates the process. So `capacity > max_trie_depth` is an invariant of the trie, and nothing
checked it.

## Modifications

- `ngram.cpp`: `Ngram::Ngram` rejects `capacity <= max_trie_depth`, next to the existing parameter
  checks and in the same style, so every caller of `NgramCorpus` gets the invariant.
- `trie.cpp`: `Trie::squeeze` compares against `global_lru_.size()` (the nodes it can actually
  evict) instead of `node_pool_.size() - free_node_count_` (which also counts the root). An
  over-large request now throws the existing "Insufficient node size" error instead of reading
  `back()` of an empty list.
- `speculative_hook.py`: `_handle_ngram` raises a `ValueError` naming both CLI flags, so a bad config
  fails during argument handling, before the model is loaded.
- Tests (CPU, existing files):
  - `test_ngram_corpus.py::TestNgramCorpusCapacity`: `capacity == max_trie_depth` is rejected at
    construction (fails on main: `RuntimeError not raised`); `capacity == max_trie_depth + 1` still
    works and evicts the whole trie on each later full-depth insert (the boundary of the new guard).
  - `test_server_args.py::TestNgramExternalSamArgs::test_capacity_must_exceed_max_trie_depth`:
    4/4 is rejected, 5/4 is accepted (fails on main: `ValueError not raised`).

Valid configs are unchanged (defaults: capacity 10,000,000, depth 18). No test, benchmark or script
in the repo sets a capacity at or below the depth.

## Accuracy Tests

No output change for valid configs. One NVIDIA GB10, `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, triton attention, NGRAM with
4 draft tokens, CUDA graphs off, three greedy requests (8 / 64 / 128 new tokens), main
(`d748bede96`) vs this PR:

| Config | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| capacity 4, depth 4 (warmup on) | never healthy: warmup request aborts the scheduler (`munmap_chunk(): invalid pointer`) | launcher exits in 12 s, before loading weights: `ValueError: --speculative-ngram-capacity must be greater than --speculative-ngram-max-trie-depth, got 4 and 4.` |
| capacity 5 (smallest valid), 64, and defaults | serves | identical text on 3/3 requests and identical `spec_verify_ct` for each config |

Repro:

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --attention-backend triton \
  --speculative-algorithm NGRAM --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \
  --speculative-ngram-capacity 4 --speculative-ngram-max-trie-depth 4

python3 test/registered/unit/spec/test_ngram_corpus.py TestNgramCorpusCapacity -v
python3 test/registered/unit/server_args/test_server_args.py \
  TestNgramExternalSamArgs.test_capacity_must_exceed_max_trie_depth -v
```

<details>
<summary>More checks (CPU unit tests, direct corpus repro, randomized put/get)</summary>

CPU, torch 2.13 cu130, aarch64, main = `d748bede96`:

| Check | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 3 new cases | 2 failed (`... not raised`), 1 passed | 3 passed |
| `test_ngram_corpus.py` | 42 passed | 44 passed |
| `test_server_args.py` | 301 passed | 302 passed |
| Corpus, depth 4, insert `[1..8]`, capacity 4 | SIGABRT, `munmap_chunk(): invalid pointer` | `RuntimeError` at construction |
| Same, capacity 2 | SIGABRT, `Insufficient node size ... available to release: 1, required to release: 3` (the 1 is the root) | `RuntimeError` at construction |
| Only the `squeeze` change, capacity 4 | - | clean `Insufficient node size` error (`available to release: 0`), no heap corruption |
| Randomized put/get: depth {2,3,4,6} x capacity {d-1, d, d+1, d+2, 3d, 1000} x {BFS, PROB} x vocab {3, 1000}, 200 steps | 32 invalid configs abort; 64 valid configs ok | 32 invalid configs rejected at construction; 64 valid configs give drafts identical to main |
| End to end, capacity 4 / depth 4 with `--skip-server-warmup` | `/health` 200, then the first `/generate` kills the scheduler | same `ValueError` at startup |

</details>

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: one comparison at construction, one at argument handling, and an O(1)
`std::list::size()` per `squeeze()` call.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). Not changed here: the startup error names both flags. The ngram flag table in `speculative_decoding.mdx` could state the bound, but the open docs PR #42687 edits that table.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (Accuracy above; speed not applicable.)
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

---

Credit: the startup validation and the root-counting analysis follow @wuhangxian's comment on #36495
and their PR #36506, which the idle-PR bot closed without review. This PR moves the check to
`speculative_hook.py` (where NGRAM arguments are handled today) and adds the C++ guards.

             speculative_num_steps=cfg.speculative_num_draft_tokens

         )
+    if cfg.speculative_ngram_capacity <= cfg.speculative_ngram_max_trie_depth:

+            f"{cfg.speculative_ngram_max_trie_depth}."
+        )
     if cfg.speculative_ngram_external_corpus_path is not None:

             raise ValueError(

@@ -2441,6 +2441,23 @@ def test_external_corpus_max_tokens_must_be_positive(self):
             handle_speculative_decoding(args)
         self.assertIn("external-corpus-max-tokens", str(context.exception))
 
+    def test_capacity_must_exceed_max_trie_depth(self):
+        """capacity == max_trie_depth must be rejected at startup, not abort the first request."""
+        args = self._make_dummy_ngram_args(
+            page_size=1,
+            speculative_ngram_capacity=4,
+            speculative_ngram_max_trie_depth=4,
+        )
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "--speculative-ngram-capacity"):
+            handle_speculative_decoding(args)
+
+        args = self._make_dummy_ngram_args(
+            page_size=1,
+            speculative_ngram_capacity=5,
+            speculative_ngram_max_trie_depth=4,
+        )
+        handle_speculative_decoding(args)
+
 
 class TestDecoupledSpecArgs(CustomTestCase):
     """Decoupled speculative-decoding CLI flags.

@@ -537,6 +537,26 @@ def test_old_data_evicted(self):
         )
 
 
+class TestNgramCorpusCapacity(CustomTestCase):
+    """Verify capacity > max_trie_depth: the root takes one node, a max-depth insert the rest."""
+
+    def test_capacity_equal_to_max_trie_depth_is_rejected(self):
+        """capacity == max_trie_depth must fail at construction, not abort the process on insert."""
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(
+            RuntimeError, "capacity must be greater than max_trie_depth"
+        ):
+            _make_corpus("BFS", capacity=4, max_trie_depth=4, draft_token_num=4)
+
+    def test_minimum_capacity_evicts_whole_trie(self):
+        """capacity == max_trie_depth + 1 is valid; later full-depth inserts must evict the whole trie."""
+        corpus = _make_corpus("BFS", capacity=5, max_trie_depth=4, draft_token_num=4)
+        corpus.batch_put([[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8]])
+        corpus.synchronize()
+
+        ids, _ = _batch_get(corpus, [[6, 7]])
+        self.assertEqual(ids.tolist(), [7, 8, 0, 0])
+
+
 class TestNgramCorpusIncremental(CustomTestCase):
